TITLE: Anti-bribery and sanctions
TEXT: The supplier does not offer, give or accept any bribe or improper advantage and complies with the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988 and the anti-bribery laws that apply to it. TITLE: Assignment and change of control
TEXT: Neither party may assign or transfer this contract without the other's written consent, which is not unreasonably withheld. The supplier tells the buyer within 15 days of a change of its control; the buyer may terminate the contract within 90 days after that notice if the new owner is a competitor of the buyer or a sanctioned person.

TITLE: Audit rights
TEXT: On 10 working days' notice and during working hours the buyer, its auditors and, for regulated goods, its customers or regulators may audit the supplier's relevant facilities, quality system, statutory compliance and records for this contract, during the contract and for three years after it ends. The supplier helps reasonably. Each party bears its own cost unless the audit finds an overcharge above 2% or a serious non-compliance.

TITLE: Material and casting integrity
TEXT: Each heat or lot has a chemical and mechanical test certificate; castings and forgings are checked by the non-destructive tests named in the drawing (X-ray, dye-penetrant, ultrasonic). The supplier keeps heat and lot traceability for ten years.

TITLE: Confidentiality
TEXT: Each party keeps the other's confidential information confidential during the contract and for five years after it ends (trade secrets for as long as they stay secret), uses it only for this contract, and discloses it only to employees, advisers and subcontractors who need it and are bound by equal duties, or as the law requires after notice to its owner where the law allows.

TITLE: Personal data
TEXT: Each party processes personal data under this contract in line with the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 and the other party's written instructions.

TITLE: Dispute resolution
TEXT: Disputes are referred to arbitration by a sole arbitrator appointed by agreement; the seat and venue are Bengaluru and the language is English. For contracts governed by Indian law the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 applies.

TITLE: Dispute resolution and arbitration
TEXT: Disputes are first referred to senior managers of both parties for 30 days. TITLE: Code of conduct and ESG
TEXT: The supplier follows the buyer's Supplier Code of Conduct: no child or forced labour, wages and working hours as the law requires, safe workplaces, environmental consents from the State Pollution Control Board, responsible sourcing of minerals, and yearly energy and emissions data on request. TITLE: Force majeure
TEXT: Neither party is liable for delay or failure caused by an event beyond its reasonable control, such as natural disaster, epidemic, war, a government order or a strike outside its own workforce, if it tells the other party within seven days and does what it reasonably can to limit the effect. If the event lasts more than 60 days either party may terminate the affected orders, and the buyer may buy elsewhere meanwhile.

TITLE: Governing law and forum
TEXT: This contract is governed by the laws of India. Subject to the arbitration clause, the courts at Bengaluru have exclusive jurisdiction.

TITLE: Indemnity
TEXT: The supplier indemnifies the buyer against third-party claims, and the losses and reasonable costs that follow, arising from the supplier's negligence, its breach of law, injury or damage to property caused by its people or goods, or the infringement of a third party's intellectual property by the goods or services as supplied. TITLE: Insurance
TEXT: The supplier keeps, at its own cost, commercial general liability and product liability insurance of at least INR 5 crore per occurrence, employees' compensation cover as the law requires, and, for work on the buyer's premises, professional indemnity and motor cover where relevant. It gives certificates on request and tells the buyer before a policy lapses.

TITLE: Intellectual property
TEXT: Each party keeps its pre-existing intellectual property. Drawings, specifications, tooling and data the buyer provides or pays for remain the buyer's property and are used only for the buyer's orders. TITLE: Limitation of liability
TEXT: Each party's total liability under or in connection with this contract in a contract year is limited to 100% of the annual contract value (or the value of the affected purchase orders where there is no annual value). Neither party is liable for loss of profit or indirect loss, except as stated in this clause.

TITLE: Payment terms and MSME compliance
TEXT: Payment N45 from receipt of a correct tax invoice and, where applicable, the goods receipt note or the approved service entry. TITLE: Production part approval (PPAP)

TITLE: Pricing
TEXT: Prices are agreed per call-off; this agreement fixes no volume or value commitment.

TITLE: Price variation and indexation
TEXT: Prices stay firm for the validity of the contract. A price changes only (a) through the published index, base value, formula, absorption band and reset dates named in the contract, with each reset applied from its effective date and never backdated, or (b) by an approved written amendment supported by documents showing a change in a statutory levy. A change in GST is passed on at the rate the law sets.

TITLE: Quality and certificate of conformity
TEXT: Goods conform to the drawing, specification and standards in the contract. TITLE: Volume rebate
TEXT: The supplier pays a rebate on the buyer's cumulative net purchases in each financial year at the rate of the tier reached, as set out in the rebate schedule. The supplier issues a credit note within 30 days after the end of the financial year; the buyer may set the rebate off against any amount it owes the supplier.

TITLE: Anti-bribery and sanctions

TITLE: Assignment and change of control
TEXT: Neither party may assign or transfer this contract without the other's written consent, which is not unreasonably withheld. TITLE: Audit rights
TEXT: On 10 working days' notice and during working hours the buyer, its auditors and, for regulated goods, its customers or regulators may audit the supplier's relevant facilities, quality system, statutory compliance and records for this contract, during the contract and for three years after it ends. TITLE: Confidentiality
TEXT: Each party keeps the other's confidential information confidential during the contract and for five years after it ends (trade secrets for as long as they stay secret), uses it only for this contract, and discloses it only to employees, advisers and subcontractors who need it and are bound by equal duties, or as the law requires after notice to its owner where the law allows.

TITLE: Consignment stock

TITLE: Emergency response

TITLE: Code of conduct and ESG

TITLE: Force majeure

TITLE: Insurance

TITLE: Intellectual property

TITLE: Limitation of liability

Neither party is liable for loss of profit or indirect loss, except as stated in this clause.

TITLE: Payment terms and MSME compliance

For a supplier registered as a micro or small enterprise the agreed period never exceeds 45 days from the day of acceptance or deemed acceptance (Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development Act, 2006, section 15), and interest at three times the bank rate notified by the Reserve Bank of India is payable on any delay (section 16). TITLE: Production part approval (PPAP)

TITLE: Pricing

TITLE: Price variation and indexation

A price changes only (a) through the published index, base value, formula, absorption band and reset dates named in the contract, with each reset applied from its effective date and never backdated, or (b) by an approved written amendment supported by documents showing a change in a statutory levy. A change in GST is passed on at the rate the law sets.

TITLE: Quality and certificate of conformity

A certificate of conformity (CoC) with the material test certificates (EN 10204 type 3.1 where the specification asks for it) travels with every lot. The supplier keeps its quality certificates (IATF 16949 or ISO 9001 as agreed) valid throughout, tells the buyer before any change of process, tool, material or site, and rejects nothing silently: non-conforming lots are reported within 24 hours and replaced at the supplier's cost.

TITLE: Volume rebate

The supplier issues a credit note within 30 days after the end of the financial year; the buyer may set the rebate off against any amount it owes the supplier.

TITLE: Scope

TITLE: Service levels and credits

For each month in which a service level is missed the supplier gives a service credit of 2% of that month's charges for each missed level, up to 10% of the month's charges. A missed level in three months of any six is a material breach.

TITLE: Subcontracting

TITLE: Stamp duty
TEXT: Stamp duty under the Maharashtra Stamp Act, 1958 is paid before the contract is relied on; the contract is executed on stamp paper or e-stamped as the law requires.

TITLE: Term of the duty

TITLE: Anti-bribery and sanctions

TITLE: Assignment and change of control

TITLE: Audit rights

TITLE: Confidentiality
TEXT: Each party keeps the other's confidential information confidential during the contract and for five years after it ends (trade secrets for as long as they stay secret), uses it only for this contract, and discloses it only to employees, advisers and subcontractors who need it and are bound by equal duties, or as the law requires after notice to its owner where the law allows.

TITLE: Personal data
TEXT: Each party processes personal data under this contract in line with the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 and the other party's written instructions.

TEXT: Goods are delivered to the plant and on the dates in the purchase order or delivery schedule, on the Incoterms 2020 rule stated in the contract; time is of the essence. TITLE: Dispute resolution
TEXT: Disputes are referred to arbitration by a sole arbitrator appointed by agreement; the seat and venue are Chennai and the language is English. For contracts governed by Indian law the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 applies.

TITLE: Insurance
TEXT: The supplier keeps, at its own cost, commercial general liability and product liability insurance of at least INR 5 crore per occurrence, employees' compensation cover as the law requires, and, for work on the buyer's premises, professional indemnity and motor cover where relevant. It gives certificates on request and tells the buyer before a policy lapses.

TITLE: Intellectual property
TEXT: Each party keeps its pre-existing intellectual property. Drawings, specifications, tooling and data the buyer provides or pays for remain the buyer's property and are used only for the buyer's orders. TITLE: Limitation of liability
TEXT: Each party's total liability under or in connection with this contract in a contract year is limited to 100% of the annual contract value (or the value of the affected purchase orders where there is no annual value). Neither party is liable for loss of profit or indirect loss, except as stated in this clause.

TITLE: Dispute resolution and arbitration
TEXT: Disputes are first referred to senior managers of both parties for 30 days. If unresolved, they are settled by arbitration under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 by a sole arbitrator appointed by agreement (three arbitrators where the claim exceeds INR 5 crore); the language is English. The seat and the courts are those named in the governing-law clause, or New Delhi if it names none; the courts have exclusive jurisdiction for interim relief and for enforcement. Pre-institution mediation under the Commercial Courts Act, 2015 is followed first for a commercial dispute that needs it.

TITLE: Code of conduct and ESG
TEXT: The supplier follows the buyer's Supplier Code of Conduct: no child or forced labour, wages and working hours as the law requires, safe workplaces, environmental consents from the State Pollution Control Board, responsible sourcing of minerals, and yearly energy and emissions data on request. The buyer may require a corrective action plan within 30 days of a finding.

TITLE: Force majeure
TEXT: Neither party is liable for delay or failure caused by an event beyond its reasonable control, such as natural disaster, epidemic, war, a government order or a strike outside its own workforce, if it tells the other party within seven days and does what it reasonably can to limit the effect. If the event lasts more than 60 days either party may terminate the affected orders, and the buyer may buy elsewhere meanwhile.

TITLE: Governing law and forum
TEXT: This contract is governed by the laws of India. Subject to the arbitration clause, the courts at Chennai have exclusive jurisdiction.

TITLE: Indemnity
TEXT: The supplier indemnifies the buyer against third-party claims, and the losses and reasonable costs that follow, arising from the supplier's negligence, its breach of law, injury or damage to property caused by its people or goods, or the infringement of a third party's intellectual property by the goods or services as supplied. The buyer tells the supplier promptly of a claim and lets it conduct the defence, with the buyer's consent for any settlement that affects the buyer.

TITLE: Insurance
TEXT: The supplier keeps, at its own cost, commercial general liability and product liability insurance of at least INR 5 crore per occurrence, employees' compensation cover as the law requires, and, for work on the buyer's premises, professional indemnity and motor cover where relevant. It gives certificates on request and tells the buyer before a policy lapses.

TITLE: Intellectual property
TEXT: Each party keeps its pre-existing intellectual property. Drawings, specifications, tooling and data the buyer provides or pays for remain the buyer's property and are used only for the buyer's orders. Intellectual property in bespoke deliverables paid for by the buyer vests in the buyer on payment, and the supplier grants the buyer a perpetual, royalty-free licence to use the supplier's pre-existing material embedded in them.

TITLE: Limitation of liability
TEXT: Each party's total liability under or in connection with this contract in a contract year is limited to 100% of the annual contract value (or the value of the affected purchase orders where there is no annual value). The limit does not apply to death or personal injury, fraud or wilful misconduct, breach of confidentiality, the indemnity for infringement of intellectual property, or any liability the law does not allow to be limited. Neither party is liable for loss of profit or indirect loss, except as stated in this clause.

TITLE: Liquidated damages for late delivery
TEXT: If the supplier delivers late, it pays liquidated damages of 0.5% of the value of the late goods or milestone for each week of delay, a part of a week counting as a full week, up to 10% of that value. The parties agree the amount is a genuine pre-estimate of the loss (Indian Contract Act, 1872, section 74). It does not limit the buyer's right to terminate for prolonged delay.

TITLE: Payment terms and MSME compliance
TEXT: Payment N15 from receipt of a correct tax invoice and, where applicable, the goods receipt note or the approved service entry. For a supplier registered as a micro or small enterprise the agreed period never exceeds 45 days from the day of acceptance or deemed acceptance (Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development Act, 2006, section 15), and interest at three times the bank rate notified by the Reserve Bank of India is payable on any delay (section 16). The supplier confirms its Udyam registration status in writing and tells the buyer within 30 days if it changes.

TITLE: Production part approval (PPAP)
TEXT: Before first delivery, and after any change that needs it, the supplier obtains the buyer's production part approval (PPAP) at the level the buyer names for the part, and re-submits it on the buyer's request. Problems found in the buyer's plant or in the field are answered with an 8D report within ten working days.

TITLE: Price and taxes
TEXT: Prices are in Indian rupees and exclude GST, which the supplier charges at the rate in force on the date of supply and shows on a valid tax invoice. Prices are fixed for the validity of the contract and include packing, marking and documentation. No other charge is payable unless the buyer agrees to it in writing before it arises.

TITLE: Price variation and indexation
TEXT: Prices stay firm for the validity of the contract. A price changes only (a) through the published index, base value, formula, absorption band and reset dates named in the contract, with each reset applied from its effective date and never backdated, or (b) by an approved written amendment supported by documents showing a change in a statutory levy. A change in GST is passed on at the rate the law sets.

TITLE: Quality and certificate of conformity
TEXT: Goods conform to the drawing, specification and standards in the contract. A certificate of conformity (CoC) with the material test certificates (EN 10204 type 3.1 where the specification asks for it) travels with every lot. The supplier keeps its quality certificates (IATF 16949 or ISO 9001 as agreed) valid throughout, tells the buyer before any change of process, tool, material or site, and rejects nothing silently: non-conforming lots are reported within 24 hours and replaced at the supplier's cost.

TITLE: Volume rebate
TEXT: The supplier pays a rebate on the buyer's cumulative net purchases in each financial year at the rate of the tier reached, as set out in the rebate schedule. The supplier issues a credit note within 30 days after the end of the financial year; the buyer may set the rebate off against any amount it owes the supplier.

TITLE: Stamp duty
TEXT: Stamp duty under the Indian Stamp Act, 1899 as amended for Tamil Nadu is paid before the contract is relied on; the contract is executed on stamp paper or e-stamped as the law requires.

TITLE: Subcontracting
TEXT: The supplier does not subcontract any material part of the work without the buyer's written consent. It stays fully liable for its subcontractors, passes down the quality, confidentiality, anti-bribery, audit and data protection terms of this contract, and replaces a subcontractor the buyer reasonably objects to.

TITLE: GST and tax compliance
TEXT: The supplier issues a valid tax invoice (with an e-invoice reference where required), files its GST returns on time so that the buyer can claim input tax credit, and keeps its registration valid. If the buyer loses input tax credit or pays interest because the supplier did not file or pay the tax, the supplier reimburses it.

TITLE: Termination for convenience
TEXT: Either party may terminate this contract for convenience with 90 days' written notice. Orders accepted before the notice run to completion unless the buyer cancels them in writing. The buyer pays for conforming goods delivered and services accepted up to the termination date and for agreed, unavoidable work in progress, and nothing else.

TITLE: Termination for cause
TEXT: Either party may terminate this contract at once by written notice if the other (a) commits a material breach that it does not cure within 30 days of written notice, (b) becomes insolvent or is the subject of a corporate insolvency resolution process under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016, or (c) in the supplier's case, breaches the anti-bribery, sanctions or code-of-conduct clauses. Termination does not affect rights that have already arisen.

TITLE: Warranty
TEXT: Goods are new, of merchantable quality and free from defects in material, workmanship and (where the supplier designed them) design, and conform to the specification, for 24 months from delivery or 18 months from first use, whichever ends first. The supplier repairs or replaces defective goods free of charge, including freight and the buyer's reasonable line-stoppage and sorting cost; replaced goods carry a new warranty.

TITLE: Anti-bribery and sanctions
TEXT: The supplier does not offer, give or accept any bribe or improper advantage and complies with the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988 and the anti-bribery laws that apply to it. It keeps accurate records, discloses any conflict of interest, does not deal with a sanctioned person on this contract, and reports a suspected breach at once. A breach is a material breach.

TITLE: Assignment and change of control
TEXT: Neither party may assign or transfer this contract without the other's written consent, which is not unreasonably withheld. The supplier tells the buyer within 15 days of a change of its control; the buyer may terminate the contract within 90 days after that notice if the new owner is a competitor of the buyer or a sanctioned person.

TITLE: Audit rights
TEXT: On 10 working days' notice and during working hours the buyer, its auditors and, for regulated goods, its customers or regulators may audit the supplier's relevant facilities, quality system, statutory compliance and records for this contract, during the contract and for three years after it ends. The supplier helps reasonably. Each party bears its own cost unless the audit finds an overcharge above 2% or a serious non-compliance.

TITLE: Confidentiality
TEXT: Each party keeps the other's confidential information confidential during the contract and for five years after it ends (trade secrets for as long as they stay secret), uses it only for this contract, and discloses it only to employees, advisers and subcontractors who need it and are bound by equal duties, or as the law requires after notice to its owner where the law allows.

TITLE: Personal data
TEXT: Each party processes personal data under this contract in line with the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 and the other party's written instructions.

TITLE: Delivery and tolerance
TEXT: Goods are delivered to the plant and on the dates in the purchase order or delivery schedule, on the Incoterms 2020 rule stated in the contract; time is of the essence. Each delivery may vary by +2% / -3% of the ordered quantity. Deliveries more than five days early may be returned or held at the supplier's risk and cost.

TITLE: Warranty

TITLE: Anti-bribery and sanctions

TITLE: Assignment and change of control

TITLE: Audit rights

TITLE: Confidentiality

TITLE: Stamp duty
TEXT: Stamp duty under the Indian Stamp Act, 1899 as amended for Tamil Nadu is paid before the contract is relied on; the contract is executed on stamp paper or e-stamped as the law requires.

TITLE: Subcontracting
TEXT: The supplier does not subcontract any material part of the work without the buyer's written consent. It stays fully liable for its subcontractors, passes down the quality, confidentiality, anti-bribery, audit and data protection terms of this contract, and replaces a subcontractor the buyer reasonably objects to.

TITLE: GST and tax compliance
TEXT: The supplier issues a valid tax invoice (with an e-invoice reference where required), files its GST returns on time so that the buyer can claim input tax credit, and keeps its registration valid. If the buyer loses input tax credit or pays interest because the supplier did not file or pay the tax, the supplier reimburses it.

TITLE: Termination for convenience
TEXT: Either party may terminate this contract for convenience with 90 days' written notice. Orders accepted before the notice run to completion unless the buyer cancels them in writing. The buyer pays for conforming goods delivered and services accepted up to the termination date and for agreed, unavoidable work in progress, and nothing else.

TITLE: Termination for cause
TEXT: Either party may terminate this contract at once by written notice if the other (a) commits a material breach that it does not cure within 30 days of written notice, (b) becomes insolvent or is the subject of a corporate insolvency resolution process under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016, or (c) in the supplier's case, breaches the anti-bribery, sanctions or code-of-conduct clauses. Termination does not affect rights that have already arisen.

TITLE: Transit documents and proof of delivery
TEXT: Every consignment travels with a valid e-way bill and consignment note. The signed proof of delivery is sent within 48 hours; payment of freight is released only against it. Shortage or damage is recorded on the proof of delivery and claimed within 30 days.

TITLE: Warranty
TEXT: Goods are new, of merchantable quality and conform to the specification for 12 months from delivery; services are performed with reasonable skill and care. Defective goods are repaired or replaced, and defective services re-performed, free of charge.

TITLE: Anti-bribery and sanctions
TEXT: The supplier does not offer, give or accept any bribe or improper advantage and complies with the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988 and the anti-bribery laws that apply to it. It keeps accurate records, discloses any conflict of interest, does not deal with a sanctioned person on this contract, and reports a suspected breach at once. A breach is a material breach.

TITLE: Assignment and change of control
TEXT: Neither party may assign or transfer this contract without the other's written consent, which is not unreasonably withheld. The supplier tells the buyer within 15 days of a change of its control; the buyer may terminate the contract within 90 days after that notice if the new owner is a competitor of the buyer or a sanctioned person.

TITLE: Audit rights
TEXT: On 10 working days' notice and during working hours the buyer, its auditors and, for regulated goods, its customers or regulators may audit the supplier's relevant facilities, quality system, statutory compliance and records for this contract, during the contract and for three years after it ends. The supplier helps reasonably. Each party bears its own cost unless the audit finds an overcharge above 2% or a serious non-compliance.

TITLE: Confidentiality
TEXT: Each party keeps the other's confidential information confidential during the contract and for five years after it ends (trade secrets for as long as they stay secret), uses it only for this contract, and discloses it only to employees, advisers and subcontractors who need it and are bound by equal duties, or as the law requires after notice to its owner where the law allows.

TITLE: Data location and exit
TEXT: The buyer's data is stored in India unless the buyer agrees otherwise in writing. At the end of the contract the supplier returns the data in an open format within 30 days and then deletes it and confirms the deletion.

TITLE: Personal data
TEXT: Each party processes personal data under this contract in line with the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 and the other party's written instructions.

TITLE: Delivery and tolerance
TEXT: Goods are delivered to the plant and on the dates in the purchase order or delivery schedule, on the Incoterms 2020 rule stated in the contract; time is of the essence. Each delivery may vary by +0% / -0% of the ordered quantity. Deliveries more than five days early may be returned or held at the supplier's risk and cost.

TITLE: Dispute resolution
TEXT: Disputes are referred to arbitration by a sole arbitrator appointed by agreement; the seat and venue are Chennai and the language is English. For contracts governed by Indian law the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 applies.

TITLE: Dispute resolution and arbitration
TEXT: Disputes are first referred to senior managers of both parties for 30 days. If unresolved, they are settled by arbitration under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 by a sole arbitrator appointed by agreement (three arbitrators where the claim exceeds INR 5 crore); the language is English. The seat and the courts are those named in the governing-law clause, or New Delhi if it names none; the courts have exclusive jurisdiction for interim relief and for enforcement. Pre-institution mediation under the Commercial Courts Act, 2015 is followed first for a commercial dispute that needs it.

TITLE: Code of conduct and ESG
TEXT: The supplier follows the buyer's Supplier Code of Conduct: no child or forced labour, wages and working hours as the law requires, safe workplaces, environmental consents from the State Pollution Control Board, responsible sourcing of minerals, and yearly energy and emissions data on request. The buyer may require a corrective action plan within 30 days of a finding.

TITLE: Force majeure
TEXT: Neither party is liable for delay or failure caused by an event beyond its reasonable control, such as natural disaster, epidemic, war, a government order or a strike outside its own workforce, if it tells the other party within seven days and does what it reasonably can to limit the effect. If the event lasts more than 60 days either party may terminate the affected orders, and the buyer may buy elsewhere meanwhile.

TITLE: Governing law and forum
TEXT: This contract is governed by the laws of India. Subject to the arbitration clause, the courts at Chennai have exclusive jurisdiction.

TITLE: Indemnity
TEXT: Each party indemnifies the other against third-party claims caused by its negligence or breach of law, subject to the limitation of liability clause.

TITLE: Information security and incident reporting
TEXT: The supplier keeps an information security programme in line with ISO/IEC 27001, tells the buyer of a security incident that affects the buyer's data without delay and in any case within six hours of becoming aware, as the CERT-In directions of 28 April 2022 require, and cooperates in the investigation.

TITLE: Insurance
TEXT: The supplier keeps, at its own cost, commercial general liability and product liability insurance of at least INR 5 crore per occurrence, employees' compensation cover as the law requires, and, for work on the buyer's premises, professional indemnity and motor cover where relevant. It gives certificates on request and tells the buyer before a policy lapses.

TITLE: Intellectual property
TEXT: Each party keeps its pre-existing intellectual property. Drawings, specifications, tooling and data the buyer provides or pays for remain the buyer's property and are used only for the buyer's orders. Intellectual property in bespoke deliverables paid for by the buyer vests in the buyer on payment, and the supplier grants the buyer a perpetual, royalty-free licence to use the supplier's pre-existing material embedded in them.

TITLE: Limitation of liability
TEXT: Liability is capped at 150% of the annual contract value; loss of profit and indirect loss are excluded.

TITLE: Liquidated damages for late delivery
TEXT: If the supplier delivers late, it pays liquidated damages of 0.5% of the value of the late goods or milestone for each week of delay, a part of a week counting as a full week, up to 10% of that value. The parties agree the amount is a genuine pre-estimate of the loss (Indian Contract Act, 1872, section 74). It does not limit the buyer's right to terminate for prolonged delay.

TITLE: Payment terms and MSME compliance
TEXT: Payment N30 from receipt of a correct tax invoice and, where applicable, the goods receipt note or the approved service entry. For a supplier registered as a micro or small enterprise the agreed period never exceeds 45 days from the day of acceptance or deemed acceptance (Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development Act, 2006, section 15), and interest at three times the bank rate notified by the Reserve Bank of India is payable on any delay (section 16). The supplier confirms its Udyam registration status in writing and tells the buyer within 30 days if it changes.

TITLE: Price and taxes
TEXT: Prices are in Indian rupees and exclude GST, which the supplier charges at the rate in force on the date of supply and shows on a valid tax invoice. Prices are fixed for the validity of the contract and include packing, marking and documentation. No other charge is payable unless the buyer agrees to it in writing before it arises.

TITLE: Price variation and indexation
TEXT: Prices stay firm for the validity of the contract. A price changes only (a) through the published index, base value, formula, absorption band and reset dates named in the contract, with each reset applied from its effective date and never backdated, or (b) by an approved written amendment supported by documents showing a change in a statutory levy. A change in GST is passed on at the rate the law sets.

TITLE: Quality and certificate of conformity

A certificate of conformity (CoC) with the material test certificates (EN 10204 type 3.1 where the specification asks for it) travels with every lot. TITLE: Rates
TEXT: Rates may be revised once a year on the anniversary by up to 5%, with 60 days' written notice and the buyer's approval.

TITLE: Volume rebate

For each month in which a service level is missed the supplier gives a service credit of 2% of that month's charges for each missed level, up to 10% of the month's charges. A missed level in three months of any six is a material breach.

TITLE: Stamp duty
TEXT: Stamp duty under the Karnataka Stamp Act, 1957 is paid before the contract is relied on; the contract is executed on stamp paper or e-stamped as the law requires.

TITLE: Subcontracting
TEXT: The supplier does not subcontract any material part of the work without the buyer's written consent. It stays fully liable for its subcontractors, passes down the quality, confidentiality, anti-bribery, audit and data protection terms of this contract, and replaces a subcontractor the buyer reasonably objects to.

TITLE: GST and tax compliance
TEXT: The supplier issues a valid tax invoice (with an e-invoice reference where required), files its GST returns on time so that the buyer can claim input tax credit, and keeps its registration valid. If the buyer loses input tax credit or pays interest because the supplier did not file or pay the tax, the supplier reimburses it.

TITLE: Termination for convenience
TEXT: Either party may terminate this contract for convenience with 90 days' written notice. Orders accepted before the notice run to completion unless the buyer cancels them in writing. The buyer pays for conforming goods delivered and services accepted up to the termination date and for agreed, unavoidable work in progress, and nothing else.

TITLE: Termination for cause
TEXT: Either party may terminate this contract at once by written notice if the other (a) commits a material breach that it does not cure within 30 days of written notice, (b) becomes insolvent or is the subject of a corporate insolvency resolution process under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016, or (c) in the supplier's case, breaches the anti-bribery, sanctions or code-of-conduct clauses. Termination does not affect rights that have already arisen.

TITLE: Warranty
TEXT: Goods are new, of merchantable quality and conform to the specification for 12 months from delivery; services are performed with reasonable skill and care. Defective goods are repaired or replaced, and defective services re-performed, free of charge.

TITLE: Anti-bribery and sanctions
TEXT: The supplier does not offer, give or accept any bribe or improper advantage and complies with the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988 and the anti-bribery laws that apply to it. It keeps accurate records, discloses any conflict of interest, does not deal with a sanctioned person on this contract, and reports a suspected breach at once. A breach is a material breach.

TITLE: Assignment and change of control
TEXT: Neither party may assign or transfer this contract without the other's written consent, which is not unreasonably withheld. The supplier tells the buyer within 15 days of a change of its control; the buyer may terminate the contract within 90 days after that notice if the new owner is a competitor of the buyer or a sanctioned person.

TITLE: Audit rights
TEXT: The buyer has no right to audit the supplier's premises, records or subcontractors.

TITLE: Confidentiality
TEXT: Each party keeps the other's confidential information confidential during the contract and for five years after it ends (trade secrets for as long as they stay secret), uses it only for this contract, and discloses it only to employees, advisers and subcontractors who need it and are bound by equal duties, or as the law requires after notice to its owner where the law allows.

TITLE: Consignment stock
TEXT: Where the supplier holds consignment stock at the buyer's plant it stays the supplier's property until it is drawn, the buyer takes reasonable care of it, counts it each quarter and pays for it 45 days after the month in which it was drawn.

TITLE: Personal data
TEXT: Each party processes personal data under this contract in line with the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 and the other party's written instructions.

TITLE: Delivery and tolerance
TEXT: Goods are delivered to the plant and on the dates in the purchase order or delivery schedule, on the Incoterms 2020 rule stated in the contract; time is of the essence. Each delivery may vary by +0% / -0% of the ordered quantity. Deliveries more than five days early may be returned or held at the supplier's risk and cost.

TITLE: Dispute resolution
TEXT: Disputes are referred to arbitration by a sole arbitrator appointed by agreement; the seat and venue are Mumbai and the language is English. For contracts governed by Indian law the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 applies.

TITLE: Dispute resolution and arbitration
TEXT: Disputes are first referred to senior managers of both parties for 30 days. If unresolved, they are settled by arbitration under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 by a sole arbitrator appointed by agreement (three arbitrators where the claim exceeds INR 5 crore); the language is English. The seat and the courts are those named in the governing-law clause, or New Delhi if it names none; the courts have exclusive jurisdiction for interim relief and for enforcement. Pre-institution mediation under the Commercial Courts Act, 2015 is followed first for a commercial dispute that needs it.

TITLE: Emergency response
TEXT: For breakdown calls the supplier responds within four hours and delivers or attends within 24 hours, at the rates in the contract, with no premium for out-of-hours calls.

TITLE: Code of conduct and ESG
TEXT: The supplier follows the buyer's Supplier Code of Conduct: no child or forced labour, wages and working hours as the law requires, safe workplaces, environmental consents from the State Pollution Control Board, responsible sourcing of minerals, and yearly energy and emissions data on request. The buyer may require a corrective action plan within 30 days of a finding.

TITLE: Force majeure
TEXT: Neither party is liable for delay or failure caused by an event beyond its reasonable control, such as natural disaster, epidemic, war, a government order or a strike outside its own workforce, if it tells the other party within seven days and does what it reasonably can to limit the effect. If the event lasts more than 60 days either party may terminate the affected orders, and the buyer may buy elsewhere meanwhile.

TITLE: Genuine spares and availability
TEXT: Spares and consumables are genuine, from the original manufacturer or its authorised channel, and the supplier keeps them available for at least seven years from the date of supply of the equipment.

TITLE: Governing law and forum
TEXT: This contract is governed by the laws of India. Subject to the arbitration clause, the courts at Mumbai have exclusive jurisdiction.

TITLE: Indemnity
TEXT: The buyer indemnifies the supplier against all third-party claims arising from the use of the goods, including claims caused by defects.

TITLE: Insurance
TEXT: The supplier keeps, at its own cost, commercial general liability and product liability insurance of at least INR 5 crore per occurrence, employees' compensation cover as the law requires, and, for work on the buyer's premises, professional indemnity and motor cover where relevant. It gives certificates on request and tells the buyer before a policy lapses.

TITLE: Intellectual property
TEXT: Each party keeps its pre-existing intellectual property. Drawings, specifications, tooling and data the buyer provides or pays for remain the buyer's property and are used only for the buyer's orders. Intellectual property in bespoke deliverables paid for by the buyer vests in the buyer on payment, and the supplier grants the buyer a perpetual, royalty-free licence to use the supplier's pre-existing material embedded in them.

TITLE: Limitation of liability
TEXT: Each party's total liability under or in connection with this contract in a contract year is limited to 100% of the annual contract value (or the value of the affected purchase orders where there is no annual value). The limit does not apply to death or personal injury, fraud or wilful misconduct, breach of confidentiality, the indemnity for infringement of intellectual property, or any liability the law does not allow to be limited. Neither party is liable for loss of profit or indirect loss, except as stated in this clause.

TITLE: Liquidated damages for late delivery
TEXT: If the supplier delivers late, it pays liquidated damages of 0.5% of the value of the late goods or milestone for each week of delay, a part of a week counting as a full week, up to 10% of that value. The parties agree the amount is a genuine pre-estimate of the loss (Indian Contract Act, 1872, section 74). It does not limit the buyer's right to terminate for prolonged delay.

TITLE: Payment terms and MSME compliance
TEXT: Payment N15 from receipt of a correct tax invoice and, where applicable, the goods receipt note or the approved service entry. For a supplier registered as a micro or small enterprise the agreed period never exceeds 45 days from the day of acceptance or deemed acceptance (Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development Act, 2006, section 15), and interest at three times the bank rate notified by the Reserve Bank of India is payable on any delay (section 16). The supplier confirms its Udyam registration status in writing and tells the buyer within 30 days if it changes.

TITLE: Price and taxes
TEXT: Prices are in Indian rupees and exclude GST, which the supplier charges at the rate in force on the date of supply and shows on a valid tax invoice. Prices are fixed for the validity of the contract and include packing, marking and documentation. No other charge is payable unless the buyer agrees to it in writing before it arises.

TITLE: Price variation and indexation
TEXT: Prices stay firm for the validity of the contract. A price changes only (a) through the published index, base value, formula, absorption band and reset dates named in the contract, with each reset applied from its effective date and never backdated, or (b) by an approved written amendment supported by documents showing a change in a statutory levy. A change in GST is passed on at the rate the law sets.

TITLE: Quality and certificate of conformity
TEXT: Goods conform to the drawing, specification and standards in the contract. A certificate of conformity (CoC) with the material test certificates (EN 10204 type 3.1 where the specification asks for it) travels with every lot. The supplier keeps its quality certificates (IATF 16949 or ISO 9001 as agreed) valid throughout, tells the buyer before any change of process, tool, material or site, and rejects nothing silently: non-conforming lots are reported within 24 hours and replaced at the supplier's cost.

TITLE: Rates
TEXT: Rates are per unit as listed on the contract lines and fixed for the contract term unless revised by an approved amendment. No rate applies that is not on the rate card, and time and expenses are payable only if the buyer approved them in writing before they were incurred.

TITLE: Volume rebate
TEXT: The supplier pays a rebate on the buyer's cumulative net purchases in each financial year at the rate of the tier reached, as set out in the rebate schedule. The supplier issues a credit note within 30 days after the end of the financial year; the buyer may set the rebate off against any amount it owes the supplier.
